claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl powder with a particle size range of 15–45 μm produces acceptable-quality but inadequately thick coatings with the standard HVAF-i7 nozzle.
Redesigning the HVAF-i7 accelerator-channel geometry will increase particle velocity.
Setting the spray distance to 300–350 mm will boost particle velocity.
Increased particle velocity will increase particle kinetic and impact energy.
Higher impact energy will improve splat flattening.
Improved splat flattening will improve interparticle bonding.
Improved particle flattening and interparticle bonding will promote the buildup of a thicker coating.
The redesigned nozzle and 300–350 mm spray distance will produce a denser FeCoNiCrAl coating.
The redesigned nozzle and 300–350 mm spray distance will produce a better-adhered FeCoNiCrAl coating.
The proposed process will maintain controlled or minimal oxidation during in-flight deposition.
Relative to the standard HVAF-i7 nozzle, the revised nozzle will yield a significantly thicker bond coat.
The resulting bond coat will maintain mechanical integrity during high-temperature service.
The resulting bond coat will maintain oxidation resistance during high-temperature service.
The thickness enhancement will remain effective in internal geometries as small as 120 mm in diameter.
The thickness enhancement will remain effective throughout a 300–350 mm spray-distance range.
Excessive particle velocity may cause unwanted oxidation or microstructural changes.
The magnitude of the thickness improvement depends on balancing increased particle velocity against oxidation risk.

contradictions.description: The proposal requires a 300–350 mm torch-to-substrate spray distance while also claiming applicability to coating inside a 120 mm-ID component. For direct spraying of an internal cylindrical wall, the available radial distance is less than 60 mm. No axial, angled, or remote-nozzle arrangement is specified that would reconcile these geometric requirements.
